name: Fight Source DE
_comment_group: One more show under the Snapchat heading. The heading names the
network these frames are cut FOR and the channel is the show they are
cut from, so another show cutting for the same network is one more
folder under it rather than a heading of its own.
Like every channel under this heading it is a frame fetcher rather
than a thumbnail maker: a video goes in and a numbered grid of
vertical stills comes out, each captioned with what was being said
over it.
It is cut to Hall of Femme's design, and that pack is the one to read
first: the frame fetch, the 540x960 vertical output, the
transcription, the rewrite that turns speech into report, the stated
40px, the twenty characters to a line, the freeform text box and the
drag and the card are all the same and are named here rather than
restated. Where it parts company with Hall of Femme is the face, the
colours, and a highlight that picks words out by colour alone rather
than by a second weight.
The DE in the name is the account's, the way the DE in Hall of Femme
DE and Fitness Story DE is: it says which of the brand's feeds this
is and not what language the app is in. What lands on the frames is
whatever the video's own voice track was saying, put through the
transcription and the rewrite exactly as on every channel here;
nothing in this pack changes that, and everything the app itself says
is English like the rest of it (see CLAUDE.md).
The glyph check the two DE feeds before this one made a habit of, and
this face passes it with one footnote. Korolev Bold carries 365
codepoints, the umlauts, the eszett and the low quotes German sets
speech in among them, so a caption is drawn from the file rather than
from whatever the browser substitutes for a missing glyph - which
would be a different face at a width nothing measured. The footnote is
the capital eszett: U+1E9E is not in the file, and is never asked for,
because the preset's `uppercase` goes through toUpperCase (see `cased`
in js/text.js) and JavaScript maps a lower-case eszett to SS rather
than to its capital. A face chosen for how it looks in English is not
automatically a face that can SET another language, and the check is
two minutes against a cmap.
A separate folder rather than a second colourway of Fight Source, for
the reason Hall of Femme DE is a folder of its own: the person picking
a channel at the top of the app picks this or that one and never both,
and these two do not merely disagree about colour. Fight Source is
white or black type on a card in the other colour, set in an italic;
this is a dark plum among its colours, in an upright display bold,
picking words out by colour rather than by cut. That is further apart
than any two packs under this heading that could ever have shared a
folder.
_comment_order: Last under the heading, which is where a new show goes: the numbers
are a running order rather than a ranking, and the foreign feeds have
been landing at the end of it since Hall of Femme DE took 920. 924
was taken by Re-belle between this pack being written and being
saved, which is the one thing a shared number costs - the server
breaks a tie alphabetically by name (see serve.py) and would have put
this above it for no reason anybody chose.
_comment_capture: The frame fetch, whole, from content/presets/snapchat-capture.json:
the slider's range, the 540x960 output, the transcription, and the
rewrite that turns it from speech into report. This channel has
nothing to say about any of it that its neighbours do not.
_comment_title: What separates this show from the others under the heading: it is set
in Korolev Bold, in a dark plum, a black or a white the user pairs per
frame, on a card, with picked words set apart by a colour the user
chooses rather than by a second face.
Everything else - the size, where the lines break, the capitals, the
freeform box, where the block stands on the frame, the drag, the shape
of the card, the word highlight - is the Snapchat caption design and
is stated once, in content/presets/snapchat-caption.json. This pack
states what makes it this show.
It used to set the caption on the photograph, in the plum alone, and
wrote down that a dark still was the one frame it would lose - and
that the honest remedies were a card or a second colour. The show has
asked for both: colours for the letters AND for a ground behind them,
which is a request for a card, since the panel palette cannot exist
without one (see editor.paletteOf). So it is on the card its carded
siblings use, and what follows from that is written once, in
content/README.md, under 'A channel that set its caption on the
photograph may take the card back'.
It also costs nothing in shape. Korolev Bold is narrow for its weight
- twenty capitals come out around 389px of the 486px a line has (see
content/faces/korolev-bold.json, which measures it) - so the preset's
twenty characters, and not the width of the frame, is still what
decides where a line breaks. That is the arithmetic the whole heading
is built on: one rewritten caption of eighty characters is four lines
of twenty, and one screen of the account fills one block.
Uppercased, for the reason every one of its neighbours is: at 40px
with twenty characters to a line the caption is three short beats
rather than a paragraph, and capitals are what those are set in. This
face has a lower case and nobody would call it the brand - Korolev's
capitals are what the family is drawn around.

_comment_color: The dark plum, and the channel's own answer: what every frame is
set in until somebody presses a swatch, since a frame stores no
colour of its own until it is given one (see state.textColorFor).
It opens the list in `colors` below, so the plum swatch is the one
shown as chosen on an untouched frame.
A near-black plum is dark type, and on the photograph a dark still
was the frame it lost. On a card it is read against a ground
somebody chose instead, which is the whole of why the card it
opens on is the white one (see `panel` below).
_comment_colors: The show's plum, then the black and the white it asked for,
offered for the letters and for the card behind them - three
buttons each in the title panel (see editor.renderColorButtons).
The same three in both lists and in one order, which is what Hall
of Femme does and for its reason: the point is the PAIRING. Plum on
white is what the show opens on; white on black and white on plum
are a button away. Plum on black is a pairing the list allows and
nobody will keep - the user can see the caption has gone and

_comment_shadow: None, and now for the preset's own reason: there is a card under
these letters and a shadow would only smear the inside of it.
Restated rather than inherited because this pack used to state it
for a different reason - a black shadow under dark type on a
photograph is darkness behind darkness - and somebody comparing
versions should find the key where it was.
_comment_highlight: The preset's word highlight, set in the block's own face and its
own plum. Picked words are told apart by COLOUR, and the colour is
the user's, from the highlight row every palette now carries.
This show used to have none, and the reason was that a highlight
would have had to split a colour inside one sentence - which was
an argument against the pack choosing that colour, not against the
user doing so. The highlight row answers it: until it is pressed
on a frame, a picked word looks exactly like its neighbours and
follows the letters' colour, so a caption nobody picks words out
of still reads as the one flat voice it was, on footage that is
already shouting. Written down once, for all nine packs that made
this change, in content/README.md under 'Every palette offers the
_comment_panel: White, and the fill is the one thing about the card this pack
decides: its shape, its padding, its corners and its shadow are
the Snapchat caption design and come from the preset.

asked for: plum on black is dark type on a dark ground, which is
the exact frame this caption used to lose on the photograph (see
`color` above). The white is the second colour asked for and the
